To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of xanthan gum and AlCl3 or Al2(SO4)3 is a promising approach for the containment of organic solvents in the subsurface.
the use of xanthan/salt solutions, gelled in situ by gaseous or by liquid acid, can be an effective method for the containment of petroleum-derived products in the subsurface.

(1) the gel layer formed by xanthan gum in presence of Al(III), generated by the reaction with gaseous carbon dioxyde, is able to contain a hydrocarbon in the porous medium, (2) the gel layer is formed in a time that depends on the thickness of the gel layer, (3) the rate of formation is faster in the presence of an external electric field.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the kinetics of the gel formation and the determination of the gel properties in the presence of organic solvents, in order to evaluate their use in the field of remediation of contaminated soils.
a novel technique for creating in situ gels for the temporary containment of oil spills.
the development of a method for containing organic solvents, such as crude oil, which may enter in the subsurface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
xanthan/aluminate solutions can be used as gels for temporarily containing oil spills in the subsurface.

both systems can be used for the in situ gelation of xanthan gum, but the gelling induced by CO(2) is more practical, since the gelation takes place without the need of adding any other chemical substance.

the gelling system xanthan/aluminate/CO(2) is more suitable for the containment of organic solvents in porous media, while the system xanthan/AlCl(3) may be used for the treatment of water polluted by organic solvents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gelling systems we propose are very promising and that the gel layers they produce have a very high resistance to the penetration of oil and other organic products.
both gelling systems can be considered as a promising technique for the containment of organic solvents and of petroleum-derived products, which may reach the subsurface.
the gelation in situ using xanthan/salts solutions is possible and that the gel layer progressively thickens as CO(2), or AlCl(3), diffuse into the polymer solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gelation of xanthan/aluminate solutions can be induced in situ by CO(2) and that the gel layer progressively grows as the gas penetrates into the xanthan/aluminium solution, thus allowing the containment of the organic liquid.
the gelation process is not instantaneous and the rate of gelation depends on the initial concentration of Al(III).
the rate of gelation is very fast, so that the time needed for the gel to be formed is very short, even for thick gel layers.
